requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The only production change is in `TypeCollector.cs`, and it stops the analyzer from crashing on bad keys. After reporting a mixed int/string key diagnostic, it now skips that member (`continue`). Before adding a member to the int-key or string-key dictionaries, it now checks whether the key already exists, so a duplicate no longer throws. Both guards are applied in two parallel member loops: the one that handles properties and the one that handles fields. The change also adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, two run-time execution tests, and a README section.
story.why: Issue 2234 reports that analyzer diagnostics stop working for types marked `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` (a regression since 3.1.1). The agent's apparent theory is that `TypeCollector` threw while analyzing such types (duplicate dictionary keys, or a null key after the mixed-kind diagnostic), which killed analysis. Nothing in the source diff mentions `SuppressSourceGeneration`. So whether this is really the root cause of the 3.1.1 regression cannot be confirmed from the diff alone.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section. It documents analyzer behaviour (MsgPack004/005/015/003/012 reported; MsgPack011/016/017 not reported) that the diff mostly does not implement or test.
A new execution test file checks that no formatter is generated for a suppressed type and that it round-trips through the dynamic resolver. This is run-time behaviour, not the analyzer.
The duplicate-key guard and the mixed-key `continue` also apply to normal (non-suppressed) types, so the source-generator path changes too: the first duplicate wins instead of throwing.
story.confidence_overview: High that the guards prevent `ArgumentException` on duplicate keys and the null dereference on mixed key kinds in the property loop; the tests exercise these. Medium-to-low that this is the actual fix for the reported regression: the diff shows no suppression-specific logic, and the positive analyzer tests may or may not have failed before the change. The field-loop copies of the fix (lines 1148, 1163-1166) have no test.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: The property loop received three fixes (lines 1008, 1023-1026, and 1039-1042), whereas the field loop only received two (continue at line 1148 and !intMembers.ContainsKey at lines 1163-1166) and omitted the !stringMembers.ContainsKey guard in the string-key else branch starting at lines 1168-1170. Consequently, duplicate string keys involving fields still throw ArgumentException in stringMembers.Add, and no tests in SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs exercise the field loop changes, so the requirement is only partly met.

No changed source line references `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The fix only prevents crashes on duplicate or mixed-kind keys. The diff does not show that this is why the analyzer stopped working for suppressed types in 3.1.1, nor that the tests for MsgPack004/015/003 (which have no duplicates) failed before this change. The reported regression may be unaddressed, or may have been fixed elsewhere.

The field-loop fixes (lines 1148 and 1163-1166) are not exercised by any test; every new test uses properties. The string-key path in the field loop (line 1170 onward) is not visibly guarded either, though it may already check `ContainsKey` before adding.

On duplicate keys, the first member now silently wins in the generated object info, where previously an exception was thrown. This is acceptable only if MsgPack005 is an error severity that blocks the build; otherwise a generated formatter could silently drop a member.

`SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed` asserts only that no diagnostics appear. It would also pass if the analyzer ignored suppressed types entirely, which is exactly the reported bug, so on its own it does not guard the requirement.
The README claims MsgPack012 (type accessibility) is still reported for suppressed types, but no test covers it and the diff does not implement it.

In the field loop's string-key else branch (starting at line 1168, checking stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) at line 1170), stringMembers.Add was not wrapped in an if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) guard, unlike the property loop at lines 1039-1042 and the field int-key branch at lines 1163-1166. Duplicate string keys on two fields (or shared between a property and a field) will still throw ArgumentException and fail the analyzer/generator, and none of the new duplicate-key tests cover fields.

No production changes in TypeCollector.cs touch SuppressSourceGeneration or rules MsgPack003, MsgPack004, MsgPack012, or MsgPack015 (only MsgPack005 duplicate/mixed-key crashes were fixed), yet REQ-2234 reports that the analyzer stopped working when SuppressSourceGeneration = true in v3.1.1. Because VerifyCS (CSharpCodeFixVerifier<MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, ...>) instantiates MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer directly in-memory rather than testing Roslyn [DiagnosticAnalyzer] discovery or the incremental generator pipeline, non-MsgPack005 tests here would pass even without this PR's code changes and will miss a real-build regression if MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer is not invoked during normal compilation.
